Translations.Explanation: Large integers and decimals is studied here as part of UAE MoE Mathematics Grade 6 — General — Term 1. Mathematical reasoning connects representations, properties and operations. Define the quantities, choose a valid method, and explain why each step preserves the required relationship. Translations.CommonMistakes: Do not use additive differences when a multiplicative comparison is required. Check units before forming a rate. Also avoid copying a procedure from a superficially similar question without checking that the same conditions apply.

The lesson develops conceptual understanding first, then connects the idea to symbolic, graphical or contextual representations. Students should explain why a method works, not only reproduce a procedure.

Record assumptions and units, keep equivalent steps explicit, and use a second representation or inverse relationship when possible to verify the result.
Translations.WorkedExamples: Worked example 1: 3/4 + 1/8 = 6/8 + 1/8 = 7/8. Worked example 2: Two thirds of 18 is (2/3) × 18 = 12. In each case, identify the mathematical relationship before calculating and finish by checking whether the result is reasonable.
